subject: maths
title: Primary 3 Bar Graphs
seo_title: P3 Bar Graphs Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Reading and interpreting data from bar graphs; using different scales on the axis
meta_desc: Free P3 maths: read bar graphs with scales of 1, 2, 5 and 10, horizontal bar graphs, compare and total data, word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Check what the scale counts by, then read across from the end of the bar.
key_sub: If the scale counts by 10s and a bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, it shows 35.
body_html:
How to read a bar graph

A bar graph uses bars to show numbers. Read it in three steps. 1. Read the title and the labels. 2. Find what the scale counts by: 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s. 3. Go from the end of the bar straight across to the scale, and read the number.

Example 1

How many more students chose apples than bananas?

Apple: 12. Banana: 7. How many more means subtract: 12 − 7 = 5.

Answer: 5 more students

Different scales

Each line on the scale is not always 1. If the scale counts by 10s, the 3rd line is 30, not 3. A bar that ends halfway between 50 and 60 shows 55.

Some bar graphs are horizontal. The bars go across, and the scale is at the bottom. Read them in the same way.

Example 2

How many more books were borrowed on Wednesday than on Friday?

Wednesday: 70. Friday: 20. The model shows the difference: 70 − 20 = 50.

Answer: 50 more books

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the grid lines as 1 eachRead the numbers on the scale: 10, 20, 30 …
Reading the bar next doorPut your finger on the right bar, then go across
Reading a bar between two lines as the line below or aboveHalfway between 30 and 40 is 35
Adding when the question asks how many moreHow many more or fewer means subtract
Stopping after step 1Read the question again: what does it ask for?

faq.q: What do P3 students learn about bar graphs?
faq.a: In Primary 3, students read and interpret bar graphs, including graphs whose scale counts by 2s, 5s or 10s and horizontal bar graphs. They use the data to compare, find totals and solve word problems.

faq.q: How do I help my child read a bar graph with a scale?
faq.a: Ask your child to read the numbers on the scale first and say what it counts by. Then put a finger on the end of the bar and go straight across to the scale.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with bar graphs?
faq.a: The most common mistake is counting each grid line as 1 when the scale counts by 2s, 5s or 10s. Reading the bar next door and misreading bars that end between two lines are also common.

faq.q: Are bar graphs in the MOE Primary 3 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Reading and interpreting data from bar graphs, using different scales on the axis, is part of Statistics in the MOE 2021 Primary 3 Mathematics syllabus. Data analysis skills like these are used all the way to the PSLE in Primary 6.

items.q: What is the title of this bar graph?
items.e: The title is at the top of the graph. It tells us what the graph is about: “How we go to school”. “Way” and “Students” are the labels on the two axes.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph count by?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 1, 2, 3 … Each line is 1 more than the one before it, so the scale counts by 1s.

items.q: How many students chose bananas?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Banana bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Banana ends on the line for 10. (9 is the bar next to it, Apple. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which bar shows 7 stickers?
items.e: The scale counts by 1s. Find 7 on the scale. The bar for Siti ends on the line for 7.

items.q: How many students chose papaya?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Papaya bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Papaya ends on the line for 8. (4 is the bar next to it, Orange. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which bar shows the most students?
items.e: The tallest bar is Bus. The bar for Bus ends on the line for 9.

items.q: How many stickers did Siti collect?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Siti bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Siti ends on the line for 2. (3 is the bar next to it, Raju. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest students?
items.e: The shortest bar is Orange. The bar for Orange ends on the line for 1.

items.q: Which bar shows 4 students?
items.e: The scale counts by 1s. Find 4 on the scale. The bar for Bicycle ends on the line for 4.

items.q: How many bars show more than 5 stickers?
items.e: Read every bar: Siti 7, Ethan 6, Mei Ling 4, Raju 3, Ali 5. More than 5 means 5 itself does not count. More than 5: Siti and Ethan. That is 2 bars.

items.q: How many students walk to school?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Walk bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Walk ends on the line for 4. (9 is the bar next to it, Bicycle. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which list matches this bar graph? The numbers are in order from left to right: Apple, Papaya, Grapes, Orange.
items.e: The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Apple ends on the line for 8. The bar for Papaya ends on the line for 2. The bar for Grapes ends on the line for 3. The bar for Orange ends on the line for 9. (2, 8, 3, 9 swaps the first two bars.)

items.q: How many students cycle to school?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Bicycle bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Bicycle ends on the line for 5. (9 is the bar next to it, MRT. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Stickers collected: Ali 6, Siti 9, Raju 4, Devi 7. Which bar graph shows this data?
items.e: C matches every number. In A, two bars are the wrong way round; in B, the Devi bar is one line too high; in D, the Ali bar is one line too low.

items.q: Which bar shows 6 students?
items.e: The scale counts by 1s. Find 6 on the scale. The bar for Banana ends on the line for 6.

items.q: Which list orders the bars from the most stickers to the fewest?
c: Mei Ling, Ali, Ethan, Siti, Raju
Siti, Raju, Ethan, Ali, Mei Ling
Raju, Ethan, Siti, Ali, Mei Ling
Raju, Siti, Ethan, Ali, Mei Ling
items.e: Read every bar: Siti 8, Ethan 6, Ali 5, Raju 10, Mei Ling 1. Start with the tallest bar and end with the shortest: Raju, Siti, Ethan, Ali, Mei Ling. (Mei Ling, Ali, Ethan, Siti, Raju goes from the fewest to the most.)

items.q: How many students take the MRT to school?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the MRT bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for MRT ends on the line for 4. (2 is the bar next to it, Car. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which bar shows the most stickers?
items.e: The tallest bar is Siti. The bar for Siti ends on the line for 10.

items.q: How many students chose oranges?
items.e: Look straight across from the end of the Orange bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Orange ends on the line for 10. (9 is the bar next to it, Apple. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: How many bars show fewer than 8 stickers?
items.e: Read every bar: Siti 7, Mei Ling 6, Ali 8, Ethan 10. Fewer than 8 means 8 itself does not count. Fewer than 8: Siti and Mei Ling. That is 2 bars.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph count by?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before it, so the scale counts by 2s. Do not count the lines as 1 each.

items.q: How many books were borrowed on Wednesday?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for Wed ends on the line for 20. (10 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: How many rainy days were there in July?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for Jul ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. (10 and 12 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: Which bar shows 14 students?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Find 14 on the scale. The bar for Choir ends on the line for 14.

items.q: Which list matches this bar graph? The numbers are in order from left to right: May, Jun, Jul, Aug.
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for May ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. The bar for Jun ends halfway between 16 and 18, so it shows 17. The bar for Jul ends on the line for 10. The bar for Aug ends on the line for 8. (8, 16, 10, 8 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph count by?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before it, so the scale counts by 5s. Do not count the lines as 1 each.

items.q: How many boxes were sold on Thursday?
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. The bar for Thu ends on the line for 20. (4 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: How many books were borrowed on Thursday?
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. The bar for Thu ends on the line for 35. (7 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: Which bar shows 20 cups?
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. Find 20 on the scale. The bar for Taro ends on the line for 20.

items.q: A bar graph has a scale that counts by 5s. The bar for mango tea ends on the 7th line above 0. What number does the bar show?
items.e: Count up the lines by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So the bar shows 35. (7 counts the grid lines as 1 each.)

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph count by?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 10, 20, 30 … Each line is 10 more than the one before it, so the scale counts by 10s. Do not count the lines as 1 each.

items.q: How many boxes were sold on Friday?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Fri ends on the line for 100. (10 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: How many points did Green House get?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Green ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. (30 and 40 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: Which bar shows 80 cups?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Find 80 on the scale. The bar for Milk tea ends on the line for 80.

items.q: How many points did Red House get?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Red ends halfway between 40 and 50, so it shows 45. (40 and 50 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: A bar graph has a scale that counts by 10s. The bar for Blue House ends on the 6th line above 0. What number does the bar show?
items.e: Count up the lines by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. So the bar shows 60. (6 counts the grid lines as 1 each.)

items.q: How many rainy days were there in April?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for Apr ends halfway between 14 and 16, so it shows 15. (14 and 16 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: Which list matches this bar graph? The numbers are in order from left to right: Art, Robotics, Football, Choir.
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. The bar for Art ends on the line for 10. The bar for Robotics ends on the line for 25. The bar for Football ends on the line for 45. The bar for Choir ends on the line for 50. (2, 5, 9, 10 counts the grid lines as 1 each.)

items.q: Which list matches this bar graph? The numbers are in order from left to right: Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat.
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Tue ends on the line for 30. The bar for Wed ends on the line for 20. The bar for Thu ends on the line for 90. The bar for Fri ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25. The bar for Sat ends on the line for 80. (30, 20, 90, 20, 80 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

items.q: Which bar shows 19 books?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Find 19 on the scale. The bar for Thu ends halfway between 18 and 20, so it shows 19.

items.q: How many more students chose grapes than apples?
items.e: Grapes: 10. Apple: 3. How many more means find the difference: 10 − 3 = 7. (13 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many students cycle or walk?
items.e: Bicycle: 10. Walk: 8. Altogether means add: 10 + 8 = 18. (2 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: How many fewer books were borrowed on Monday than on Wednesday?
items.e: Wed: 16. Mon: 10. How many fewer means find the difference: 16 − 10 = 6. (26 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many students are in these CCAs altogether?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Read every bar: Art: 20, Football: 4, Choir: 16, Dance: 11. Add them all: 20 + 4 + 16 + 11 = 51. Make sure you add every bar once. (50 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

items.q: How many more cups of peach tea than taro tea were sold?
items.e: Peach: 50. Taro: 10. How many more means find the difference: 50 − 10 = 40. (60 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many more stickers does the tallest bar show than the shortest bar?
items.e: The tallest bar is Siti (7). The shortest bar is Raju (1). 7 − 1 = 6.

items.q: How many boxes were sold on Wednesday and Monday altogether?
items.e: Wed: 35. Mon: 30. Altogether means add: 35 + 30 = 65. (5 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: How many more points did Green House get than Red House?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Green: 90. Red: 30. How many more means find the difference: 90 − 30 = 60. (120 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many rainy days were there in the other months, not counting June?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Add the other bars: 15 + 10 + 8 + 16 = 49. Or find the total, 63, and take away Jun (14): 63 − 14 = 49.

items.q: How many fewer cups of peach tea than mango tea were sold?
items.e: Mango: 50. Peach: 20. How many fewer means find the difference: 50 − 20 = 30. (70 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many books were borrowed altogether?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Read every bar: Mon: 40, Tue: 80, Wed: 50, Thu: 25, Fri: 100. Add them all: 40 + 80 + 50 + 25 + 100 = 295. Make sure you add every bar once. (290 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

items.q: How many more stickers must Ali collect to have as many as Siti?
items.e: Siti: 10. Ali: 7. Find the difference: 10 − 7 = 3. (10 is Siti’s number, not how many more.)

items.q: How many more students does the tallest bar show than the shortest bar?
items.e: The tallest bar is Choir (50). The shortest bar is Dance (15). 50 − 15 = 35.

items.q: How many points did Red House and Blue House get altogether?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Red: 75. Blue: 60. Altogether means add: 75 + 60 = 135. (15 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: How many students are in the survey altogether?
items.e: Read every bar: Walk: 4, Bicycle: 1, Car: 6, Bus: 2, MRT: 8. Add them all: 4 + 1 + 6 + 2 + 8 = 21. Make sure you add every bar once.

items.q: The bar for August is not drawn yet. The total is 57 days. What number should the August bar show?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 15 + 16 + 14 = 45. Then 57 − 45 = 12. So the Aug bar should end at 12.

items.q: How many fewer boxes were sold on Thursday than on Monday?
items.e: Mon: 100. Thu: 80. How many fewer means find the difference: 100 − 80 = 20. (180 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many books were borrowed on the other days, not counting Friday?
items.e: Add the other bars: 35 + 25 + 20 = 80. Or find the total, 130, and take away Fri (50): 130 − 50 = 80.

items.q: How many more boxes does the Tuesday bar show than the Monday and Wednesday bars together?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Step 1: Mon and Wed together: 30 + 35 = 65. Step 2: Tue: 90. 90 − 65 = 25. (65 stops after step 1.)

items.q: Which bar shows twice as many cups as the Mango bar?
items.e: Mango: 15. Twice as many is 2 × 15 = 30. The Milk tea bar shows 30.

items.q: How many students chose prata?
items.e: Look straight down from the end of the Prata bar to the scale. The scale counts by 1s. The bar for Prata ends on the line for 7. (8 is the bar next to it, Satay. Keep your finger on the right bar.)

items.q: Which bar shows the most students?
items.e: The longest bar is Grapes. The bar for Grapes ends on the line for 10.

items.q: How many students chose nasi lemak?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for Nasi lemak ends on the line for 12. (6 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: How many students joined football?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. The bar for Football ends halfway between 14 and 16, so it shows 15. (14 and 16 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: How many more students chose laksa than nasi lemak?
items.e: Laksa: 10. Nasi lemak: 2. How many more means find the difference: 10 − 2 = 8. (12 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph count by?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before it, so the scale counts by 5s. Do not count the lines as 1 each.

items.q: How many students chose satay?
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. The bar for Satay ends on the line for 25. (5 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: Which bar shows 35 students?
items.e: The scale counts by 5s. Find 35 on the scale. The bar for Art ends on the line for 35.

items.q: How many students chose laksa or nasi lemak?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Laksa: 6. Nasi lemak: 20. Altogether means add: 6 + 20 = 26. (14 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: How many points did Blue House get?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Blue ends on the line for 20. (2 counts the grid lines as 1 each. Read the number on the scale instead.)

items.q: How many students chose chicken rice?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Chicken rice ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. (60 and 70 are the lines on each side of it.)

items.q: How many fewer books were borrowed on Tuesday than on Thursday?
items.e: Thu: 45. Tue: 20. How many fewer means find the difference: 45 − 20 = 25. (65 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest points?
items.e: The shortest bar is Yellow. The bar for Yellow ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35.

items.q: How many rainy days were there in these months altogether?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Read every bar: May: 16, Jun: 12, Jul: 18, Aug: 11. Add them all: 16 + 12 + 18 + 11 = 57. Make sure you add every bar once. (56 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

items.q: How many more cups of mango tea than milk tea were sold?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Mango: 100. Milk tea: 70. How many more means find the difference: 100 − 70 = 30. (170 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many more students does the longest bar show than the shortest bar?
items.e: The longest bar is Satay (45). The shortest bar is Nasi lemak (5). 45 − 5 = 40.

items.q: Which bar shows 9 days?
items.e: The scale counts by 2s. Find 9 on the scale. The bar for Aug ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9.

items.q: Each student voted once. How many students did not choose laksa?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Add the other bars: 85 + 90 + 40 = 215. Or find the total, 275, and take away Laksa (60): 275 − 60 = 215.

items.q: The bar for Milk tea is not drawn yet. The total is 115 cups. What number should the Milk tea bar show?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 35 + 25 + 10 + 30 = 100. Then 115 − 100 = 15. So the Milk tea bar should end at 15.

items.q: Which list matches this bar graph? The numbers are in order from top to bottom: Green, Red, Blue, Yellow.
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. The bar for Green ends on the line for 30. The bar for Red ends on the line for 20. The bar for Blue ends on the line for 100. The bar for Yellow ends halfway between 80 and 90, so it shows 85. (30, 20, 100, 80 reads the bars between two lines as the line below.)

sets.title: Word problems: fruit, books and more

items.q: How many more P3 students chose melon than papaya?
items.e: The scale counts by 10s. Melon ends on 50. Papaya ends halfway between 10 and 20, so 15. 50 − 15 = 35. (40 reads papaya as 10, and 30 reads it as 20.)

items.q: How many P3 students chose a fruit altogether?
items.e: Apple 45, banana 30, papaya 15, melon 50, grapes 25. 45 + 30 + 15 + 50 + 25 = 165. (150 reads every bar between two lines as the line below; 140 leaves out grapes.)

items.q: The canteen vendor gives 1 fruit to each student who chose apple or grapes. How many fruits does she need?
items.e: Apple 45 (halfway between 40 and 50). Grapes 25 (halfway between 20 and 30). 45 + 25 = 70. (20 subtracts instead of adding. 60 reads both bars as the line below.)

items.q: The bananas come in bunches of 5. How many bunches are needed so that each student who chose banana gets 1 banana?
items.e: Banana ends on the line for 30, so 30 students need 30 bananas. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 bunches. (25 subtracts 5, and 150 multiplies by 5.)

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Twice as many chose banana as papaya.
Grapes and papaya are the same.
Apple is the most popular fruit.
items.e: Banana 30 and papaya 15: 2 × 15 = 30, so twice as many chose banana. Melon (50) is the most popular, not apple (45). Grapes (25) and papaya (15) are different.

items.q: On which day were the most books borrowed?
items.e: The longest bar is Thursday. It ends halfway between 80 and 90, so 85 books.

items.q: How many fewer books were borrowed on Friday than on Thursday?
items.e: Thursday 85 (halfway between 80 and 90). Friday 30. 85 − 30 = 55. (Reading Thursday as 80 gives 50, as 90 gives 60. 115 adds them.)

items.q: How many books were borrowed from Monday to Friday?
items.e: 40 + 65 + 50 + 85 + 30 = 270. (260 reads Tuesday as 60 and Thursday as 80. 240 leaves out Friday.)

items.q: Mrs Lim hoped for 300 books to be borrowed this week. How many more books were needed to reach 300?
items.e: Step 1: total borrowed: 40 + 65 + 50 + 85 + 30 = 270. Step 2: 300 − 270 = 30 more books. (40 and 20 come from reading the bars between two lines wrongly: 300 − 260 and 300 − 280.)

items.q: On which two days were 90 books borrowed altogether?
items.e: Monday 40 + Wednesday 50 = 90. (Tuesday and Friday: 65 + 30 = 95. Monday and Friday: 70. Wednesday and Friday: 80.)

items.q: Next term, 10 of the students who come by car will take the bus instead. How many students will take the bus then?
items.e: Bus now: 40. 10 more will take the bus: 40 + 10 = 50. (20 is the new number of car students: 30 − 10.)

items.q: Which two ways together have the same number of students as the bus?
items.e: Bus: 40. Walk 25 + MRT 15 = 40. (MRT and Car: 45. Walk and Car: 55.)

items.q: Mr Tan says, “More than half of these students take the bus.” Is he right?
c: Yes. The bus bar is the longest.
No. 40 is less than half of 110.
items.e: Total: 25 + 40 + 15 + 30 = 110. Half of 110 is 55. Only 40 take the bus. The longest bar shows the most popular way, not more than half.

items.q: Mei Ling collected 24 stickers. Raju collected 9 more stickers than Mei Ling. How many stickers did they collect altogether?
items.e: Step 1: Raju: 24 + 9 = 33. Step 2: altogether: 24 + 33 = 57. (33 is only Raju’s stickers. Stop only when you have answered the question.)

items.q: In a bar graph of books borrowed, the bar for Week 1 shows 150 books. The bar for Week 2 is 3 times as long. How many books were borrowed in Week 2?
items.e: 1 unit = 150. Week 2 is 3 units: 3 × 150 = 450 books. (153 adds 3. 600 is both weeks together.)

items.q: In a class survey, twice as many students chose apple as banana. 36 students chose apple or banana. How many students chose apple?
items.e: Apple is 2 units and banana is 1 unit. 3 units = 36, so 1 unit = 36 ÷ 3 = 12. Apple: 2 units = 2 × 12 = 24. (12 is banana. 18 halves 36, but there are 3 units, not 2.)

items.q: A bubble tea shop sold 85 cups of milk tea. It sold 37 fewer cups of taro tea. How many cups of taro tea did it sell?
items.e: Taro is shorter by 37. 85 − 37 = 48. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 − 7 = 8, 7 − 3 = 4. (52 takes 5 − 7 as 7 − 5. 122 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: On Sports Day, Red House got 240 points. Blue House got 75 more points than Red House. Green House got 50 fewer points than Blue House. How many points did Green House get?
items.e: Step 1: Blue: 240 + 75 = 315. Step 2: Green: 315 − 50 = 265. (315 is Blue House. 190 takes 50 from Red House instead of Blue House. 365 adds the 50 instead of subtracting.)

items.q: In a survey, 64 students chose apple. This is 16 more than the number who chose papaya. How many students chose apple or papaya?
items.e: Papaya is 16 fewer than apple: 64 − 16 = 48. Altogether: 64 + 48 = 112. (144 adds 16 to get papaya, but papaya is the smaller bar. 48 is only papaya.)

items.q: Hui Min drew a bar graph of the books she read. She read 18 books in June. In July she read 6 fewer books than in June. In August she read twice as many books as in July. How many books did she read in August?
items.e: Step 1: July: 18 − 6 = 12. Step 2: August is 2 units of 12: 2 × 12 = 24. (36 doubles June instead of July. 12 is July.)
